stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Slide $E$, $r$ and $R$. Both panels drive the same load $R$ — the Thévenin source ($E$ in series with $r$) and the Norton source ($I_0 = E/r$ in parallel with $r$) always yield identical terminal readings $U$ and $I$.
stages.concept: Any linear two-terminal network is equivalent to a voltage source $E$ in series with an internal resistance $r$ (Thévenin) — or, equivalently, a current source $I_0 = E/r$ in parallel with the same $r$ (Norton). External behavior is the same.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: $E$ and $r$ are locked. Adjust $R$ so the terminal voltage $U$ hits each of the three target values in sequence. Watch the Norton panel: it reports the same $U$ and $I$ for every $R$.
stages.concept: Terminal voltage: $U = E - r \cdot I = R \cdot I$. Solving: $I = E / (R + r)$, so $U = E \cdot R / (R + r)$. The Norton form gives the same result: $U = R \cdot (I_0 - U/r)$ rearranges to the same expression.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The source is a sealed black box. Two operating points $(R, I, U)$ are given. Compute $E$ and $r$ on paper, then enter them. 3 attempts per scenario — ace 3 scenarios in a row.
stages.concept: From two points on the line $U = E - r \cdot I$: slope $-r = (U_2 - U_1) / (I_2 - I_1)$, so $r = (U_1 - U_2) / (I_2 - I_1)$. Intercept: $E = U_1 + r \cdot I_1$. The Norton parameter follows: $I_0 = E / r$.

labels.tip1: move E, r and R; watch both panels stay in agreement
labels.tip2: adjust R only — E and r are fixed for this stage
labels.tip3: napkin math first, then commit — no live meter to guess against
labels.peek_tip: Two points on the line $U = E - r I$: slope $-r = (U_2 - U_1)/(I_2 - I_1)$, intercept $E = U_1 + r I_1$.

1.1: Try sliding E first. Then r. Both panels update together.
1.2: For any (E, r, R), the Thévenin and Norton panels give the same terminal U and I. They are equivalent representations of the same source.
1.3: The Norton current source magnitude is I₀ = E / r. Change E and watch I₀ track it.

2.1: Only R moves this stage. E and r are fixed at the shown values.
2.2: Terminal voltage: U = E · R / (R + r). Set R for each target.
2.3: For U = 6 V with E = 12 V, r = 2 Ω: 6 = 12·R/(R+2) → R = 2 Ω. Apply the same for U = 8 V and U = 10 V.

3.1: Draw the line U(I) from the two given points. Its slope is −r; its y-intercept (I = 0) is E.
3.2: r = (U₁ − U₂) / (I₂ − I₁). Once you have r, substitute back to find E.
3.3: Method: compute r from the ΔU/ΔI ratio, then E = U₁ + r · I₁. Both fields are checked with ±3% tolerance.
